item.title: Quantum-HPC Workflows Across Multiple Quantum Computing Platforms: Two Case Studies
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Demonstrated end-to-end multi-QPU Quantum-HPC workflow orchestrating Fugaku, Quantinuum Reimei, and ibm_kobe via Tierkreis. Combined VQE (ibm_kobe) and QPE (Reimei) achieved energy error (E−Eexact)/J=0.61±0.36.

Grade 0.379 · 2.2σ above the day's baseline · matched “quantum chemistry and electronic structure on quantum computers” · Philipp Seitz, Miwako Tsuji, John Children, Yuta Kikuchi, Riku Masui, Juan Pedersen, Kentaro Yamamoto, Ross Duncan

Figure

Estimated ground state energy (E−Eexact)/J versus QPE iteration count k, comparing the hybrid VQE+QPE hardware run against exact ground state and pure VQE baselines.

Asks

How can hybrid Quantum-HPC applications across multiple distinct QPU modalities and classical supercomputing platforms be orchestrated systematically via a unified workflow management system?

Before

VQE alone yielded (E−Eexact)/J=2.47±0.10 on hardware and 1.25±0.15 in noiseless simulation.

But

4×4 transverse-field Ising model with h=3J, periodic boundary conditions, D=2 VQE layers over 500 SPSA iterations, and NSQPE=300 shots with kmax⁡=20.

Tools

Tierkreis workflow management system · Fugaku supercomputer · Quantinuum Reimei (trapped-ion QPU) · ibm_kobe (superconducting QPU) · sqcsub submission framework

Abstract

We describe the Quantum-HPC hybrid system comprising the supercomputer Fugaku, the QPUs Quantinuum Reimei and ibm_kobe, and the Tierkreis hybrid workflow software. We present two demonstrations of the system at work. In the first, we compute the excited states of a biomolecular system using Fugaku and Reimei (simulator) to handle classical and quantum parts of the workflow respectively. In the second, Fugaku coordinates Reimei and ibm_kobe working together in a combined VQE + QPE workflow to compute the ground state energy of a simple system.

item.title: Non-abelian quantum cellular automata: 1+1-dimensional SU(2) Yang--Mills with fermions
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Formulated the first discrete-spacetime quantum cellular automaton simulation algorithm for 1+1-dimensional SU(2) Yang-Mills theory coupled to massive Dirac fermions, recovering the standard Hamiltonian in the ε→0 continuum limit.

Grade 0.375 · 2.1σ above the day's baseline · matched “lattice gauge theory simulation on quantum hardware” · Dogukan Bakircioglu, Pablo Arrighi

Figure

Quantum circuit architecture showing the alternating sequence of local swap 𝐒x, coin 𝐂x, and multi-qubit controlled gauge-covariant transfer operations 𝐓x over discrete time steps.

Asks

How to formulate non-abelian SU(2) Yang-Mills lattice gauge theory with fermions as an explicitly unitary, gauge-covariant digital quantum cellular automaton?

But

Restricted to 1+1 dimensions without magnetic plaquette terms; requires truncation of infinite-dimensional L2(SU(2)) gauge-link Hilbert space for actual quantum circuits; continuum convergence proof remains a sketch.

Tools

quantum cellular automata · pointwise product of gauge links · compound matrix multi-particle lifting · discrete Gauss law projection

Abstract

This work provides a digital quantum simulation scheme for 1+1-dimensional SU(2) Yang--Mills theory with Dirac fermions. It takes the form of a quantum circuit, infinitely repeating across space and time with Δ_t=Δ_x=ε, whose wires follow lightlike propagation. The construction mirrors the logic of the standard quantum field theory approach, transposed to the discrete setting. Namely, we start from the Dirac quantum walk, restore SU(2) gauge symmetry by introducing the gauge field, lift the walk to a multi-particle QCA while preserving fermionic anticommutation, and equip the gauge field with its own dynamics. Rather than relying on Clebsch--Gordan decompositions, we use the pointwise-product structure of gauge-link updates, which yields self-contained proofs of unitarity and gauge covariance in quantum-computing notation. The construction provides an explicit algorithmic formulation of the theory, whose continuum limit we discuss.

item.title: Quantum algorithms for the exponentiation of Toeplitz matrices and applications in partial differential equations
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Constructs quantum algorithms for matrix exponentiation of banded Toeplitz matrices by decomposing lower and upper shift operators into circulant and skewcirculant generators diagonalised via QFT, enabling block encoding of heat equation propagators across periodic, Dirichlet, and Neumann boundary conditions with a frequency cutoff.

Grade 0.353 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “analog quantum simulation of lattice models on cold atoms or superconducting ar…” · Xabier Gutiérrez, Nicola Mariella, Javier González-Conde, Sergiy Zhuk, Mikel Sanz

Asks

How to efficiently implement the quantum matrix exponential of banded Toeplitz matrices despite potentially large matrix norms.

But

Applies specifically to banded Toeplitz matrices and discretised heat equation propagators subject to frequency cutoffs.

Tools

LCU-based block encoding · circulant and skewcirculant decomposition · Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) · Pauli-string truncation · QFT-Trotter product formula

Abstract

We present quantum algorithms to approximate the exponential of banded Toeplitz matrices. These matrices have central importance in many PDE related problems, but their quantum implementation is hindered by their possibly large norms. Constructing directly the exponential we can circumvent this limitation. By relating the lower/upper shift operators to circulant and skewcirculant generators, which are diagonalised by the QFT, we construct (i) an LCU-based block encoding of banded Toeplitz matrices, (ii) an efficient, controllably truncated Pauli-string decomposition of the circulant eigenphases with a closed-form error bound, and (iii) a specialized QFT-Trotter product formula. As an application we build a block encoding of the propagator of the discretised heat equation with periodic, Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, using a frequency cutoff.

item.title: A Novel q-Derivative Framework with Applications to q-Deformed Thermodynamics and Leakage Suppression in Superconducting Qubits
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Formulates q-derivative Dxqf(x)=q−1ln⁡(q)df(x)dx, yielding consistent q-thermodynamic quantities without chain-rule modifications, and generalizes transmon DRAG pulse shaping using effective anharmonicity δq=ω0(q+q−1−2) to enable fidelities F>99.99% at Tgate≈6–12 ns.

Grade 0.346 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Practical quantum advantage in quantum simulation” · André A. A. Marinho, Gisele B. Freitas, Clovis A. C. Filho

Figure

Expectation value evolution of the annihilation operator in phase space for a qutrit, comparing the undeformed oscillator (q=1.0) to the deformed case (q=1.25) exhibiting beating and precession.

Asks

How can q-calculus be formulated to preserve standard differential calculus structures and model leakage suppression in superconducting qubits?

But

Thermodynamic results evaluated in the dilute gas limit (z≪1). Quantum control derived within a three-level qutrit subspace (d=3).

Tools

Jackson q-calculus · Biedenharn-Macfarlane q-oscillator · Schrieffer-Wolff transformation · DRAG pulse shaping

Abstract

We propose a new q-derivative operator built directly from Jackson's q-number formulation, designed to preserve the structural properties of standard differential calculus while incorporating deformation effects. By analyzing q-deformed Heisenberg algebras, we demonstrate that this formulation maintains the consistency of thermodynamic quantities-such as internal energy, particle number, and specific heat-in dilute gas limits without requiring ad-hoc chain-rule modifications. Furthermore, we explore the physical implications of algebraic deformation using the Biedenharn-Macfarlane realization, showing how q-deformation induces intrinsic anharmonicity in quantum oscillator spectra and affects multi-level quantum systems (d ≥3). Applying this algebraic scheme to superconducting transmon qubits, we derive analytical pulse-shaping corrections that generalize the Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate (DRAG) technique, offering a robust method to suppress computational leakage in ultra-fast quantum logic operations.

item.title: Parallel and Distributed Fermionic Simulation via Dynamic Encoding
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Dynamic fermionic encoding via combinatorial covering designs reduces inter-QPU communication cost to 𝒪(Mr) for M fermionic modes and Trotter number r.

Grade 0.344 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Probing many-body dynamics on a 51-atom quantum simulator” · Michael Williams de la Bastida, Peter V. Coveney

Asks

How can Trotterized fermionic Hamiltonian simulation be efficiently parallelized and distributed across multiple quantum processing units with minimal communication overhead?

Before

Static encoding bound for q QPUs scaled as 𝒪(M4qr).

But

Combines best communication scaling across molecular systems except in the sparsest Hamiltonians.

Tools

Combinatorial covering designs · Dynamic fermion-qubit encoding · Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation · Hypergraph partitioning · Pauli-weight optimization

Abstract

We demonstrate a simple and efficient method to parallelize and distribute Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation of fermionic systems across multiple QPUs. Using combinatorial covering designs to define a minimal set of fermion-qubit encodings, we demonstrate communication cost scaling as O(M r) for a system of M fermionic modes and Trotter number r, improving on the static encoding bound for q QPUs, O(M⁴ q r). We compare this approach to dynamic encoding using a randomised method, Pauli-weight based optimisation and hypergraph partitioning. Applying this to the Hamiltonians of a range of molecular systems, we find the combinatorial covering approach results in the lowest communication cost in all but the sparsest Hamiltonians.

item.title: Counterdiabatic quantum optimization for efficient state preparation in the Schwinger model
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Counterdiabatic-inspired QAOA protocols prepare the ground state of the (1+1)-dimensional Schwinger model with higher approximation ratios and fidelities than standard QAOA across 4 to 10 qubits, while reducing circuit depth and operation count.

Grade 0.343 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “lattice gauge theory simulation on quantum hardware” · Ethan Laval, Bipasha Chakraborty, Stefano Cipolla

Figure

Average approximation ratio versus number of QAOA layers p for 4, 6, 8, and 10 qubits using an XY mixer. CD-inspired ansatz consistently yields higher approximation ratios across all layers and system sizes compared to standard QAOA.

Asks

Can counterdiabatic driving variants of QAOA prepare the ground state of the Schwinger model at lower circuit depths than standard QAOA?

But

Classical noise-free simulation; model parameters fixed to m=0.35, w=0.6, J=5/12, $ heta=0$; tested on systems up to 10 qubits.

Tools

DC-QAOA and CD-inspired variational circuits · CD term fixing and parameter fixing strategies · FakeAlgiers IBM backend circuit transpilation · Classical statevector simulation

Abstract

The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), whose design is underpinned by the adiabatic theorem, is one of the leading variational quantum algorithms for preparing the ground states of gauge theories. A recently proposed variant, DC-QAOA, incorporates counterdiabatic driving to accelerate the adiabatic process, reducing both circuit depth and runtime. In this work, we present a systematic analysis, from both theoretical and computational perspectives, of DC-QAOA and related counterdiabatic variants for preparing the ground state of the Schwinger model, the paradigmatic (1+1)-dimensional lattice gauge theory. Benchmarking these methods against standard QAOA, we show that counterdiabatic driving improves ground-state preparation while lowering circuit depth requirements. Our results establish counterdiabatic protocols as a practical route towards efficient quantum simulation of gauge theories.
